ee:2009:q2.title: GATE EE 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 2
ee:2009:q2.question: The measurement system shown in the figure uses three sub-systems in cascade whose gains are specified as $G_1,G_2 \; and \; \frac{1}{G_3}$. The relative small errors associated with each respective subsystem $G_1,G_2 \; and \; G_3$ are $\varepsilon _1,\varepsilon _2 \; and \; \varepsilon _3$. The error associated with the output is :

primary.subtopicLabel: Characteristics of Instruments and Measurement Systems

detailed_solution.concept: Electrical and Electronic Measurements - Characteristics of Instruments and Measurement Systems
detailed_solution.markdown:
$\frac{dG_1}{G_1}=\varepsilon  _1,$  $\frac{dG_2}{G_2}=\varepsilon  _2,$and $\frac{dG_3}{G_3}=\varepsilon  _3$

Output $(y)_0=\frac{G_1G_3}{G_3}x$

where,  $\;\; x=input$

$\ln y=\ln G_1+ \ln G_2- \ln G_3 +\ln x$

Differentiating both side,

$\frac{dy}{y}=\frac{dG_1}{G_1}+\frac{dG_2}{G_2}-\frac{dG_3}{G_3}+\frac{dx}{x}$

No error is specified in input, so $\frac{dx}{x}=0$

$\frac{dy}{y}==\varepsilon  _1+\varepsilon  _2-\varepsilon  _3$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

ee:2009:q6.title: GATE EE 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 6
ee:2009:q6.question:
A field excitation of 20 A in a certain alternator results in an armature current
of 400 A in short circuit and a terminal voltage of 2000 V on open circuit. The
magnitude of the internal voltage drop within the machine at a load current of 200 A is

detailed_solution.markdown:
If $R_a$ is neglected,

$\vec{E_f}=\vec{V_t}+j\vec{I_a}X_s$

For a given field current under short-circuit condition,

$$\begin{aligned} I_a &=I_{sc} \\ V_t&= 0\\ X_s &=\frac{E_f}{I_{sc}} \\ \text{But,}\;\; E_f &=V_{oc} \end{aligned}$$

(open circuit voltage i.e. $I_a=0$ with the same field current).

Then with the linearity assumption

$$\begin{aligned} X_s&=\left.\begin{matrix} \frac{V_{oc}}{I_{sc}} \end{matrix}\right|_{I_f=\text{constant}} \\ &= \frac{2000}{400}=5\Omega \end{aligned}$$

Internal voltage drop

$I_aX_s=200 \times 5=1000V$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

ee:2009:q9.title: GATE EE 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 9
ee:2009:q9.question:
For a fixed value of complex power flow in a transmission line having a sending
end voltage V, the real loss will be proportional to

primary.subtopicLabel: Performance of Transmission Lines, Line Parameters and Corona

detailed_solution.concept: Power Systems - Performance of Transmission Lines, Line Parameters and Corona
detailed_solution.markdown:
S= Complex power

S is defined as, S=VI

$I=\frac{S}{V}$

If R is the resistance of transmission line

Real power loss $=I^2R=\left ( \frac{S}{V} \right )^2R=\frac{S^2R}{V^2}$

Since, S and R are fixed

Real power loss $\propto \frac{1}{V^2}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

ee:2009:q10.title: GATE EE 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 10
ee:2009:q10.question:
How many 200 W/220 V incandescent lamps connected in series would consume
the same total power as a single 100 W/220 V incandescent lamp ?

detailed_solution.concept: Electric Circuits - Basics of Electric Circuit
detailed_solution.markdown:
Let resistance of a single incandescent lamp=R.

Power consumed by a single lamp, P=200W.

When connected across voltage, V=220V.

So, $P=\frac{V^2}{R}\; \Rightarrow \; 200=\frac{220^2}{R}$

$\Rightarrow \; R=242\Omega$

Let, n number of lamps are connected in series across voltage V=200V.

So total resistance of lamps

$R_{eq.}=nR=242n$

Total power consumed,

$P=\frac{V^2}{R_{eq.}}$

$\Rightarrow \; 100=\frac{220^2}{242n} \Rightarrow \; n=2$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

ee:2009:q11.title: GATE EE 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 11
ee:2009:q11.question:
A Linear Time Invariant system with an impulse response h(t) produces output
y(t) when input x(t) is applied. When the input x(t-$\tau$) is applied to a system with impulse response h(t-$\tau$), the output will be

detailed_solution.concept: Signals and Systems - Linear Time Invariant Systems
detailed_solution.markdown:
Case-1: $Y(s)=H(s) \cdot X(s)$

Case-1: input $=x(t-\tau )\Rightarrow X(s)e^{-s\tau }$

impulse response $=h(t-\tau )\Rightarrow H(s)e^{-s\tau }$

Output: $Y'(s)=X(s)e^{-s\tau }H(s)e^{-s\tau }$

$Y'(s)=X(s)H(s)e^{-2s\tau }=Y(s)e^{-2s\tau}$

$y'(t)=y(t-2 \tau)$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

ee:2009:q14.title: GATE EE 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 14
ee:2009:q14.question: The single phase, 50 Hz iron core transformer in the circuit has both the vertical arms of cross sectional area 20 $cm^2$ and both the horizontal arms of cross sectional area 10 $cm^2$. If the two windings shown were wound instead on opposite horizontal arms, the mutual inductance will

detailed_solution.markdown: Mutual inductance is where the flux of two or more coils are linked so that voltage is induced in one coil proportional to the rate of change of current in another. The mutual inductance that exist between the coils can be greatly increased by positioning them on a common soft iron core or by increasing the number of turns of either coil. Consider: The changing flux on coil 1 is proportional to changing current in coil 2. $$\begin{aligned} N_1 \frac{d\phi _{12}}{dt}&=M_{12}\frac{dI_2}{dt} \\ \Rightarrow \;\;M_{12} &=N_1 \frac{\phi _{12}}{I_2} \end{aligned}$$ Similarly time rate of change of magnetic flux $\phi _{21}$ in coil 2 is proportional to time rate of change of current in coil 1 $$\begin{aligned} N_2 \frac{d\phi _{21}}{dt}&=M_{21}\frac{dI_1}{dt} \\ \Rightarrow \;\;M_{21} &=N_2 \frac{\phi _{21}}{I_1}\\ \text{Also} \;\; M_{12}&=M_{21}=M \end{aligned}$$ We can observe that none of the parameters changes due to placing of coils on horizontal arms. Hence, mutual inductance will remain unchanged. Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

ee:2009:q15.title: GATE EE 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 15
ee:2009:q15.question: A 3-phase squirrel cage induction motor supplied from a balanced 3-phase source drives a mechanical load. The torque-speed characteristics of the motor(solid curve) and of the load(dotted curve) are shown. Of the two equilibrium points A and B, which of the following options correctly describes the stability of A and B ?
options: A is stable, B is unstable
A is unstable, B is stable

detailed_solution.markdown: Let torque developed by the motor $=T_m$ Load torque $=T_L$ Accelerating torque,$T_a=T_m-T_L$ At point A, $T_m=T_L$ $\Rightarrow \;\;T_a=T_m-T_L=0$ So, no accelerating , hence the motor rums at speed $N_A$. When a smal disturbance decreases speed to $N_c$ At point C, $T_m \gt T_L$ $\Rightarrow \;\;T_a \gt 0$ So, motor will accelerate and comes to point A. When the disturbance increases speed to $N_D$. At point D, $T_m \lt T_L$ $\Rightarrow \;\;T_a \lt 0$ Motor will decelerate and comes at point A So, motor is stable at point A. When the motor is operating at point B., $T_m = T_L$ $\Rightarrow \;\;T_a= 0$ If a small disturbance decreases speed to $N_E$. $T_m \lt T_L$ $\Rightarrow \;\;T_a \lt 0$ Motor will decelerate and motor speed will keep on decreasing. If the disturbance increases speed to $N_F$. At point F, $T_m \gt T_L$ $\Rightarrow \;\;T_a \gt 0$ Motor will accelerate and motor speed will keep on increasing. So, motor is unstable at point B. Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

ee:2009:q18.title: GATE EE 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 18
ee:2009:q18.question:
The first two rows of Routh's tabulation of a third order equation are as follows.
$$\begin{matrix} s^{3} &2 &2 \\ s^{2}& 4 &4 \end{matrix}$$
This means there are
options: Two roots at $s =\pm j$ and one root in right half s-plane
Two roots at $s =\pm j2$ and one root in left half s-plane
Two roots at $s =\pm j2$ and one root in right half s-plane
Two roots at $s = \pm j$ and one root in left half s-plane

detailed_solution.markdown: Routh-Array The third row vanishes. An auxillary equation is formed using elements pf 2nd row. Auxiliary equation $A(s)=4s^2+4=0\Rightarrow s=\pm j.$ The derivative of this auxiliary equation is taken w.r.t. s and the cofficient of the differntiated equation are taken as the elements of 3rd row. $\frac{dA(s)}{ds}=8s$ Routh-Array There is no root in RHS of s-plane. Two roots of $s=\pm j$, so one root is in LHS of s-plane. Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

ee:2009:q19.title: GATE EE 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 19
ee:2009:q19.question: The asymptotic approximation of the log-magnitude v/s frequency plot of a system containing only real poles and zeros is shown. Its transfer function is

detailed_solution.markdown:
Initial slope =-40 dB/dec.

Hence the system is type-2. So the corresponding term of the transfer function is $1/s^2$.

At $\omega =2$ rad/sec, slope changes by -20 dB/dec from -40 dB/dec to -60 dB/dec. Hence the corresponding term of the transfer function is $\frac{1}{\left ( 1+\frac{s}{2} \right )}$.

At $\omega =3$ rad/sec, slope changes by 20 dB/dec from -60 dB/dec to -40 dB/dec. Hence the corresponding term of the transfer function is $\left ( 1+\frac{s}{5} \right )$.

At $\omega =25$ rad/sec, slope changes by -20 dB/dec from -40 dB/dec to -60 dB/dec. Hence the corresponding term of the transfer function is $\frac{1}{\left ( 1+\frac{s}{25} \right )}$.

$G(s)=\frac{k\left ( 1+\frac{s}{5} \right )}{s^2\left ( 1+\frac{s}{2} \right )\left ( 1+\frac{s}{25} \right )}$

At  $\omega =0.1(\omega \leq 2 \;rad/sec)$

$Gain(dB)=20 \log k-40 \log \omega$

$80=20 \log k-40 \log 0.1$

$20 \log k=40$

$k=100$

$G(s)=\frac{100 \left ( 1+\frac{s}{5} \right )}{s^2\left ( 1+\frac{s}{2} \right )\left ( 1+\frac{s}{25} \right )} =\frac{1000(s+5)}{s^2(s+2)(s+25)}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

ee:2009:q22.title: GATE EE 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 22
ee:2009:q22.question: In the figure shown, all elements used are ideal. For time $t \lt 0$, $S_1$ remained closed and $S_2$ open. At t=0, $S_1$ is opened and $S_2$ is closed. If the voltage $V_{C2}$ across the capacitor $C_2$ at t=0 is zero, the voltage across the capacitor combination at t=$0^+$ will be

detailed_solution.concept: Electric Circuits - Transients and Steady State Response
detailed_solution.markdown: At $t=0^-, S_1$ is closed, $S_2$ is open $C_1$ gets charged upto 3 V Charge stored in $C_1$ $Q_0=C_1V=1 \times 3=3C$ Voltage across $C_2$ is zero at $t=0^-$, so no charge is stored in $C_2$. At $t \gt 0,\;S_1$ is open and $S_2$ is closed. Charge stored ($Q_0$) initially in $C_2$ gets redistributed between $C_1$ and $C_2$. Let charge stored in $C_1=Q_1$ Charge stored in $C_2=Q_1$ According to conservation of charge $Q_1+Q_2=Q_0=3\;\;...(i)$ Voltage across $C_1$ =Voltage across $C_2$ $\frac{Q_1}{C_1}=\frac{Q_2}{C_2}$ $\rightarrow \;\; \frac{Q_1}{1}=\frac{Q_2}{2}$ $Q_2=2Q_1\;\;...(ii)$ Solving equation (i) and (ii) we get $Q_1=1 C$ and $Q_2 =2 C$ Voltage across combination $= \frac{Q_1}{C_1}=\frac{1}{1}=1$ Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

ee:2009:q27.title: GATE EE 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 27
ee:2009:q27.question: The unit-step response of a unity feed back system with open loop transfer function G(s) = K/((s + 1) (s + 2)) is shown in the figure. The value of K is

detailed_solution.markdown:
Steady state value of response = 0.75

Input is unit step

So steady state error

$e_{ss}=1-0.75=0.25$

$Error=E(s)=\frac{R(s)}{1+G(s)H(s)}$

$where, \;\; G(s)=\frac{k}{(s+1)(s+2)} \;\; H(s)=1$  $R(s)=\frac{1}{s}$

Steady state erro using find value theorem,

$e_{ss}=\lim_{s \to 0}sE(s)$

$\;\;\lim_{s \to 0}\frac{sR(s)}{1+G(s)H(s)}$

$\;\;\lim_{s \to 0}\frac{s\cdot \frac{1}{s}}{1+\frac{k}{(s+1)(s+2)}}$

$\;\;=\frac{1}{1+k/2}$

$\Rightarrow\;\; 0.25=\frac{1}{1+k/2}$

$\Rightarrow \;\; k=6$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

ee:2009:q28.title: GATE EE 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 28
ee:2009:q28.question:
The open loop transfer function of a unity feed back system is given by
 $G(s) =(e^{-0.1s})/s$. The gain margin of the is system is

detailed_solution.markdown:
Open loop transfer function, $G(s)=\frac{e^{-0.1s}}{s}$

Put,  $s=j\omega$

$G(j\omega)=\frac{e^{-j0.1\omega}}{j\omega}$

At phase crossover frequency $(\omega_{pc})$, phase of OLTF is $-180^{\circ}$

$\angle G(j\omega)|_{\omega/\omega_{pc}}=-180^{\circ}=-\pi$

$-\frac{\pi}{2}-0.1\omega_{pc}=-\pi$

$-0.1\omega_{pc}=-\frac{\pi}{2}$

$\omega_{pc}=5 \pi$

$|e^{-0.1\omega}|$ is always 1 for any value of $\omega$

$|G(j\omega)|=\frac{1}{\omega }$

Gain at $\omega_{pc}$ ( phase-cross frequency)

$|G(j\omega)|_{\omega_{pc}=5 \pi}=\frac{1}{5 \pi }$

Gain margin $=20 log \frac{1}{|G(j\omega_{pc}|}$

$\;\;\;=20 log 5\pi=23.9 dB$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

ee:2009:q31.title: GATE EE 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 31

Three generators are feeding a load of 100 MW. The details of the generators are

primary.subtopicLabel: Economic Power Generation and Load Dispatch

detailed_solution.markdown:
Let $x_1,x_2 \text{ and }x_3$

are reactance of generator-1, generator-2 and generator-3 respectively.

Neglecting armature resistance of all the three generators

ee:2009:q32.question:

detailed_solution.markdown:

Synchronous speed $N_s=\frac{120f}{P}=\frac{120 \times 50}{2}=300rpm$

Kinetic energy of the rotor

$=\frac{1}{2}J\omega _s^2=\frac{1}{2}\times 27.5 \times 10^3 \times (314.16)^2$

G= Machine rating $=\frac{500}{pf}=\frac{500}{0.9}=555.55MVA$

Inertia constant $=H=\frac{K.E.}{G}=\frac{1357}{555.55}=2.44 \; MJ/MVA$

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

ee:2009:q35.title: GATE EE 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 35
ee:2009:q35.question:
A cascade of three Linear Time Invariant systems is causal and unstable. From
this, we conclude that
options: each system in the cascade is individually causal and unstable
at least on system is unstable and at least one system is causal
at least one system is causal and all systems are unstable
the majority are unstable and the majority are causal

detailed_solution.concept: Signals and Systems - Linear Time Invariant Systems
detailed_solution.markdown:
Since in cascade overall impulse response

$h(t)=h_1(t)*h_2(t)*h_3(t)$

$h_1(t),h_2(t),h_3(t)$ are impulse response of individual systems.

Since, initial point where h(t) is nonzero is $t \geq 0$ and since in convolution initial point

$=t_1+t_2+t_3$

where, $t_1,t_2,t_3$ are initial point of $h_1(t), h_2(t),h_3(t)$ respectively.

So for it to be greater than or equal to zero at least one of them $t_1, t_2\; or \; t_3$ must be +ve i.e. greater than zero so atleast one of them must be causal. Similarly if one (atleast) of the system become unstable then overall system will become unstable.

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

ee:2009:q36.title: GATE EE 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 36
ee:2009:q36.question: The Fourier Series coefficients of a periodic signal x(t), expressed as $x(t)=\sum_{k=-\infty }^{\infty }a_{k}e^{j2 \pi kt/T}$ are given by $a_{-2}=2-j1$, $a_{-1}=0.5+j0.2$, $a_{0}=j2$, $a_{1}=0.5-j0.2$, $a_{2}=2+j1$ and $a_{k}=0$ for $|k| \gt 2$ Which of the following is true ?
options: x(t) has finite energy because only finitely many coefficients are non-zero
x(t) has zero average value because it is periodic
The imaginary part of x(t) is constant
The real part of x(t) is even

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} x(t)&=a_{-2}e^{-j2\omega _0t}+a_{-1}e^{-j\omega _0t}\\ &+a_{1}e^{j\omega _0t} +a_{2}e^{j2\omega _0t}\\ &=(2-j)e^{-j2\omega _0t}+(2+j)e^{j2\omega _0t}\\ &+(0.5+j0.2)e^{-j\omega _0t}+(0.5-j0.2)e^{j\omega _0t}+2j\\ &=2(e^{-j2\omega _0t}+e^{j2\omega _0t})+j(e^{j2\omega _0t}-e^{-j2\omega _0t})\\ &+0.5(e^{j\omega _0t}+e^{-j\omega _0t})-j0.2(e^{j\omega _0t}-e^{-j\omega _0t})+2j\\ &=4 \cos 2\omega _0t-2 \sin 2\omega _0t+ \cos \omega _0t \\ &+0.4 \sin \omega _0t+2j\\ &=\text{Real}[x(t)]+j\text{Img}[x(t)]\\ &\text{where,}\\ \text{Real}[x(t)]&=4 \cos 2\omega _0t-2 \sin 2\omega _0t+ \cos \omega _0t \\ &+0.4 \sin \omega _0t\\ &= \text{neither even nor odd signal}\\ \text{Img}[x(t)]&=2=\text{constant} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

ee:2009:q37.title: GATE EE 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 37
ee:2009:q37.question:
The z-transform of a signal x[n] is given by $4z^{-3}+3z^{-1}+2-6z^{2}+2z^{3}$.
It is applied to a system, with a transfer function  $H(z) =3z^{-1}-2$.
Let the output be y(n). Which of the following is true ?
options: y(n) is non causal with finite support
y(n) is causal with infinite support

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} y[n] &=x[n]*H[n] \\ y[z]&= x[z]H[z]\\ y[z]&=(4z^{-3}+3z^{-1}+2-6z^{2}+2z^{3}) (3z^{-1}-2)\\ &=12z^{-4}+9z^{-2}+6z^{-1}-18z+6z^{2} \\ &-8z^{-3}-6z^{-1}-4+12z^{2}-4z^{3} \\ &= -4z^3+18z^2-18z+12z^{-4}+9z^{-2}-4-8z^{-3}\\ y[n]&\neq 0 \; \text{ for }n \lt 0 \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, it is noncausal with finite support.

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

ee:2009:q40.title: GATE EE 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 40
ee:2009:q40.question: $F(x,y) =(x^{2}+xy)\hat{a}_{x}+(y^{2}+xy)\hat{a}_{y}$. It's line integral over the straight line from (x,y)=(0,2) to (x,y)=(2,0) evaluates to

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} \bar{F}&=(x^2+xy)\hat{a_x}+(y^2+xy)\hat{a_y} \\ (x_1,y_1)&=(0,2) \\ (x_2,y_2)&=(2,0) \end{aligned}$$

equation of starting line $\frac{y-y_1}{x-x_1}=\frac{y_1-y_1}{x_2-x_1}\Rightarrow \;y=2-x\;\;\;dy=-dx$

$\bar{F}\cdot \bar{dl}=(x^2+xy)dx+(y^2+xy)dy$

Putting $y=2-x$ and $dy=-dx$

$\int \bar{F}\cdot \bar{dl}=\int_{0}^{2}2xdx-\int_{0}^{2}(4-2x)dx=0$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

ee:2009:q42.question: A 200 V, 50 Hz, single-phase induction motor has the following connection diagram and winding orientations as shown. Directions of the winding axis indicate direction of flux when currents in the windings are in the directions shown. Parameters of each winding are indicated. When switch S is closed, the motor

primary.subtopicLabel: Single Phase Induction Motors, Special Purpose Machines and Electromechanical Energy Conversion System

detailed_solution.concept: Electrical Machines - Single Phase Induction Motors, Special Purpose Machines and Electromechanical Energy Conversion System
detailed_solution.markdown: $f=50Hz$ Impedance of main winding $$\begin{aligned} Z_m &= r_m+j2 \pi f L_m\\ &=0.1+ j 2 \pi \times 20 \times \frac{0.1}{\pi} \\ Z_m&=0.1+j10\Omega \end{aligned}$$ Impedance of auxiliary winding, $$\begin{aligned} Z_a &=r_a+j2 \pi fL_a \\ &= 1+j 2 \pi \times 50 \times \frac{10}{\pi}\\ Z_a&= 1+j1000\Omega \end{aligned}$$ Current through main winding, $I_m=\frac{V_s}{Z_m}=\frac{220}{0.1+j10}$ $I_m=200\angle -89.427^{\circ}A$ Current through auxiliary winding $I_a=\frac{V_s}{Z_a}$ $\;\;\;=\frac{220}{1+j1000}=0.22\angle -89.942$ Thaing $V_s$ as the reference $I_m$ leads $I_a$ the field crreated by the two current also have same difference thereby constituting an unbalanced field system, The result is the production of the starting torque. Space orientation of the field The motor rotates in the direction of leading phase to lagging phase.In this case, the motor rotates anti-clockwise. Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

ee:2009:q43.title: GATE EE 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 43
ee:2009:q43.question: The circuit shows an ideal diode connected to a pure inductor and is connected to a purely sinusoidal 50 Hz voltage source. Under ideal conditions the current waveform through the inductor will look like.

primary.subtopicLabel: Power Semiconductor Devices and Commutation Techniques

detailed_solution.concept: Power Electronics - Power Semiconductor Devices and Commutation Techniques
detailed_solution.markdown:
Frequency of the voltage source, f=50Hz

Time period, $T=\frac{1}{f}=\frac{1}{50}=20ms$

During positive half cycle of the source voltage, $0 \lt t \lt \frac{T}{2}$, energy is stored in the inductor and current increases.

During negative half cycle of the source voltage, $\frac{T}{2} \leq t \leq T$, current decreases and energy stored in the inductor is delivered to source.

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

ee:2009:q44.title: GATE EE 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 44
ee:2009:q44.question: The Current Source Inverter shown in figure is operated by alternately turning on thyristor pairs ($T_1,T_2$) and ($T_3,T_4$). If the load is purely resistive, the theoretical maximum output frequency obtainable will be

detailed_solution.markdown:
The circuit shown in the figure is a single phase bridge auto sequential commutated inverter (1-phase ASCI).

Thyristor pairs $T_1,T_2 \text{ and }T_3,T_4$ are alternatively switches to obtain a nearly square wave load current. Two commutating capacitors, one $C_1$ in the upper half and the other $C_2$ in the lower half are connected as shown.

Diodes $D_1$ to $D_4$ are connected in series with each SCR to prevent the commutation capacitors from discharging into the load.

THe inverter output frequency is controlled by adjusting the period T through the triggering circuits of thyristors.

The theoretical maximum output frequency obtainable

$f_{max}=\frac{1}{4RC}=\frac{1}{4 \times 10 \times 0.1 \times 10^{-6}}=250kHz$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

ee:2009:q48.title: GATE EE 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 48
ee:2009:q48.question: The figure shows a three-phase delta connected load supplied from a 400V, 50 Hz, 3-phase balanced source. The pressure coil (PC) and current coil (CC) of a wattmeter are connected to the load as shown, with the coil polarities suitably selected to ensure a positive deflection. The wattmeter reading will be

detailed_solution.concept: Electrical and Electronic Measurements - Measurement of Energy and Power
detailed_solution.markdown:
Assuming phase angle sequence abc

Line to line voltage $V_{l-l}=400V$

Taking $V_{ab}$ as the reference

$$\begin{aligned} V_{ab} &=V_{l-l}\angle 0^{\circ}=400 \angle 0^{\circ}V\\ V_{bc}&=400\angle -120^{\circ}V \\ V_{ca} &= 400\angle -240^{\circ}V\\ \text{Current}&\text{ through current coil} \\ I{cc}&=\frac{V_{ca}}{Z_2}=\frac{400\angle -240^{\circ}}{100+j0}\\ &=4\angle -240^{\circ}A\\ \text{Voltage }&\text{ across pressure ciol}\\ V_{pc}&=V_{bc}=400\angle -120^{\circ}V \\ \phi &=\text{angle between} I_{cc} \text{and} V_{pc}\\ &=-120-(-240^{\circ})=120^{\circ}\\ \text{Wattmeter }&\text{reading,}\\ |V_{pc}||I_{cc}| \cos \phi &=400 \times 4 \times \cos (120^{\circ})\\ &=-800W \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

ee:2009:q53.title: GATE EE 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 53
ee:2009:q53.question:
The circuit diagram shows a two-winding, lossless transformer with no leakage flux, excited from a current source, i(t), whose waveform is also shown. The transformer has a magnetizing inductance of 400/$\pi$ mH.

The peak voltage across A and B, with S open is

detailed_solution.markdown: No leakage flux $\;\Rightarrow \; X_{l1} \;\text{and}\; X'_{l2}$ are neglected. Transformer is lossless $\;\Rightarrow \; R_1, R'_2 \; \text{and}\; R_c$ are neglected. $L_{\phi }=$ magnetizing inductances $=\frac{400}{\pi}mH$ Therefore, the above equivalent circuit can be redrawn with S open. $V_{AB}=L_{\phi }\frac{di(t)}{dt}$ (i) During $0 \lt t \leq 5 \; ms , i(t)$ increases linearly with time $$\begin{aligned} i(t) &=\frac{10}{5 \times 10^{-3}}t=2000t \\ V_{AB}&=L_{\phi } \frac{di(t)}{dt}\\ &= \frac{400}{\pi} \times 10^{-3} \times \frac{d(2000t)}{dt}\\ &= \frac{800 }{\pi}V \end{aligned}$$ (ii) during $5 \; ms \lt t \leq 15 \; ms$ $$\begin{aligned} i(t) &=-2000t+20 \\ V_{AB}&=L_{\phi } \frac{di(t)}{dt}\\ &= \frac{400}{\pi} \times 10^{-3} \times \frac{d}{dt}(-2000t+20)\\ &= -\frac{800 }{\pi}V \end{aligned}$$ (iii) During $150\; ms \lt t \leq 25 \; ms$ $$\begin{aligned} i(t) &=2000t-40 \\ V_{AB}&=L_{\phi } \frac{di(t)}{dt}\\ &= \frac{400}{\pi} \times 10^{-3} \times \frac{d}{dt}(2000t-40)\\ &= \frac{800 }{\pi}V \end{aligned}$$. Therefore, peak voltage across A nad B $\frac{800 }{\pi}V$ Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

ee:2009:q54.title: GATE EE 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 54
ee:2009:q54.question:
The circuit diagram shows a two-winding, lossless transformer with no leakage flux, excited from a current source, i(t), whose waveform is also shown. The transformer has a magnetizing inductance of 400/$\pi$ mH.

If the wave form of i(t) is changed to i(t)=10 sin(100$\pi$t) A, the peak voltage across A and B with S closed is

detailed_solution.markdown: When s is closed the equivalnet circuit, $$\begin{aligned} \text{Here,}\;\;R'_L &= \left ( \frac{N_1}{N_2} \right )^2 R_L\\ &= \left (\frac{1}{1} \right )^2 \times 30\\ &= 30\Omega \end{aligned}$$ Load current referred to primary side, $i'_2(t)=\frac{j\omega L_m}{j\omega L_m+R'_L} \times i(t)$ Load voltage referred to primary side, $V'_2=i'_2(t)R'_L$ $\rightarrow \;\; V'_2(t)=\frac{j\omega L_m R'_L}{j\omega L_m+R'_L} \times i(t)$ so, secondary voltage across A and B $$\begin{aligned} V_2(t) &=\frac{N_2}{N_1}V'_2(t) \\ V_2(t) &=\frac{1}{1} \times V'_2(t) \\ \Rightarrow \; V_2(t) &= \frac{j\omega L_m R'_L}{j\omega L_m+R'_L} \times i'(t) \end{aligned}$$ Given, $i(t)=10 \cos 100\pi t$ $\therefore \;$ frequency , $$\begin{aligned} \omega &= 100\pi\\ V_2(t) &=\frac{j100 \pi \times \frac{400}{\pi} \times 10^{-3} \times 30}{30+j100\pi \times \frac{400}{\pi} \times 10^{-3}} \times 10 \sin 100 \pi t \\ &= V_m \cos (100 \pi t +\phi ) \end{aligned}$$ Peak value of secondary voltage, $V_m=\left | \frac{j12000}{30+j40} \right |V=240V$ Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

ee:2009:q55.title: GATE EE 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 55
ee:2009:q55.question:
A system is described by the following state and output equations
$\frac{dx_1(t)}{dt}=-3x_1(t)+x_2(t)+2u(t)$
$\frac{dx_2(t)}{dt}=-2x_2(t)+u(t)$
$y(t)=x_1(t)$
when u(t) is the input and y(t) is the output

The system transfer function is

detailed_solution.markdown:
Selecting $x_1(t)$ and $x_2(t)$ as state variable,

$$\begin{aligned} \dot{x}_1(t)&=\frac{dx_1(t)}{dt} \\&=-3x_1(t)+x_2(t)+2u(t)  \\ \dot{x}_2(t)&=\frac{dx_2(t)}{dt} =-2x_2(t)+u(t)  \\ \begin{bmatrix} \dot{x}_1(t)\\ \dot{x}_2(t) \end{bmatrix}&=\begin{bmatrix} -3 &1\\ 0& -2 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x_1(t)\\ x_2(t) \end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix} 2\\ 1 \end{bmatrix}u(t)  \\ \dot{x}&=AX+BU \\ \text{So, } A&=\begin{bmatrix} -3 &1\\ 0& -2 \end{bmatrix}, \; B=\begin{bmatrix} 2\\ 1 \end{bmatrix}  \\ y(t)&=x_1(t)  \\ y(t)&=\begin{bmatrix} 1 &0 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x_1(t)\\ x_2(t) \end{bmatrix}  \\ y&=CX+DU \\ \text{So, } C&=\begin{bmatrix} 1 &0 \end{bmatrix} \text{ and } D=0 \\  [sI-A]&=\begin{bmatrix} s & 0\\ 0 & s \end{bmatrix}-\begin{bmatrix} -3 &1\\ 0& -2 \end{bmatrix} \\ &=\begin{bmatrix} s+3 &-1\\ 0& s+2 \end{bmatrix}  \\ [sI-A]^{-1}&=\frac{\begin{bmatrix} s+2 &1\\ 0& s+3 \end{bmatrix}}{(s+2)(s+3)} \\ &\text{Transfer function} \\ &=C[sI-A]^{-1}B+D  \\ &=\begin{bmatrix} 1 &0 \end{bmatrix}\frac{\begin{bmatrix} s+2 &1\\ 0& s+3 \end{bmatrix}}{(s+2)(s+3)}\begin{bmatrix} 2\\ 1 \end{bmatrix}+0  \\ &=\frac{\begin{bmatrix} 1 &0 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 2(s+2)+1\\ s+3 \end{bmatrix}}{(s+2)(s+3)}  \\ &=\frac{2s+5}{(s+2)(s+3)}=\frac{2s+5}{s^2+5s+6}\end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

ee:2009:q56.title: GATE EE 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 56
ee:2009:q56.question:
A system is described by the following state and output equations
$\frac{dx_1(t)}{dt}=-3x_1(t)+x_2(t)+2u(t)$
$\frac{dx_2(t)}{dt}=-2x_2(t)+u(t)$
$y(t)=x_1(t)$
when u(t) is the input and y(t) is the output

The state-transition matrix of the above system is

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$[sI-A]^{-1}=\frac{\begin{bmatrix} s+2 &1\\ 0& s+3 \end{bmatrix}}{(s+2)(s+3)}$$

$$=\begin{bmatrix} \frac{1}{s+3} & \frac{1}{(s+2)(s+3)}\\ 0 & \frac{1}{s+2} \end{bmatrix}$$

$$=\begin{bmatrix} \frac{1}{s+3} & \frac{1}{s+2}-\frac{1}{s+3}\\ 0 & \frac{1}{s+2} \end{bmatrix}$$

State transition matrix

$=L^{-1}[[sI-A]^{-1}]$

$$=L^{-1}\begin{bmatrix} \frac{1}{s+3} & \frac{1}{s+2}-\frac{1}{s+3}\\ 0 & \frac{1}{s+2} \end{bmatrix}$$

$$=\begin{bmatrix} e^{-3t} &e^{-2t}-e^{-3t} \\ 0& e^{-2t} \end{bmatrix}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.
